title: Leakage-corrected C5 noisy fused loop: CDL recovery to bounded CASM execution
question: When the clean target is hidden and CDL must operate only on a one-bit-corrupted public query, can calibrated sparse admission feed a bounded CASM verifier loop as M grows?
hypothesis: On a fixed error-correcting semantic codebook, noisy CDL outcome training should recover the relevant class with a bounded rank distribution; OR-LSH admission should preserve most of that recall at a smaller rerank fraction; verifier-gated repair should convert admitted candidates into successful actions without access to the hidden target.

arms.name: cdl_noisy_dense
arms.intervention: outcome-trained dense CDL routing on noisy query only

arms.name: cdl_noisy_sparse_casm
arms.intervention: CDL Q/K + OR-LSH + calibrated K + exact CASM + outcome verifier/repair

arms.name: persistent_clean_control
arms.intervention: separate upper-bound control reading clean target from delayed persistent state

decision_rule.condition: Report all registered M levels for Hamming, dense CDL, and sparse CDL+LSH+CASM+Verifier; do not select the reported operating point using held-out outcomes.
decision_rule.licenses: workload-specific diagnosis of representation, admission, execution, and repair bottlenecks.
decision_rule.does_not_license: general semantic capability or universal sparse scaling.

decision_rule.condition: A sublinear routing statement requires the measured query-work exponent beta to be below 1 and no LSH table cap to bind at any reported M.
decision_rule.licenses: an empirical scaling statement on the registered workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: a complexity theorem or hardware speedup.

decision_rule.condition: Conformal K is fit only on calibration trials and evaluated on a separate held-out stream; coverage is reported empirically and interpreted conditionally on exchangeability.
decision_rule.licenses: calibrated shortlist behavior under the registered sampling scheme.

decision_rule.condition: Verifier-driven success must be produced after CASM execution and may use only noisy public query, candidate data, execution trace, and environment outcome.
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that execution/verification is separated from hidden-target routing.
decision_rule.does_not_license: verification of the hidden target relation itself.

held_constant: 16-bit binary semantic codebook with 64 classes and minimum Hamming distance 3
one-bit query corruption for the main arm
M populations repeat all 64 classes equally
main router query contains only noisy bits; no address field
hidden valid-action set never enters router or verifier inputs
CASM compares candidate descriptor to the observed noisy query, not hidden target
environment exposes success only after action execution
verified experience learning occurs only after environment success and verification
LSH uses OR-over-tables random hyperplanes with table count derived from measured rho
result_note: Run 36832999287 completed successfully with 806 repository tests passing. Main noisy arm: gamma=0.775989, beta=0.465440, P90 best-valid rank 2→17 over M=64→1024, K90 2→17, held-out K90 coverage 97.5% pooled, Hamming reference 100% Top-1 at all M, sparse final success 70.0%, 73.44%, 65.94%, 67.50%, 65.31%, persistent clean control 100% and reset 0% at M=128, online final success 58.96%. The main interpretation is that noisy CDL representation is the first learned bottleneck, with OR-LSH causing a second admission loss; no general semantic or end-to-end complexity claim is licensed.
